purpose: How a certified Medicare-focused agent keeps an already-enrolled book alive, serviced and compliant after the sale: reading renewal compensation, rate-year determination and recoupment as regulated mechanisms whose current-year terms must be verified rather than remembered, holding the conditions that keep renewals payable at all, running a year-round service desk for provider, drug-cost, denial and billing events inside a strict scope of practice, conducting annual reviews that know exactly where a service conversation becomes a sales appointment, and measuring persistency and book stability so that growth comes from service quality and compliant referrals rather than from churn, pressure or compensation-driven steering.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the agent already holds an active health line license, the current plan-year certification class and the carrier appointments covering every plan in the book; that stack is the sibling certifications and marketing KB's territory and appears here only as a status this KB verifies before it acts and monitors as a condition of continued renewal payment

compensation schedules, rate-year determination rules, recoupment classes and windows, payment cadence, marketing and contact rule classes, continuity-of-care provisions and transition-supply rules change by plan year, by carrier contract and by state; every one of them is described here as a mechanism or a class and must be verified in current-year official sources, in the carrier's own current compensation schedule and contract, and against the agent's own state rules before it is used with a client or relied on for income

the people served are predominantly older adults and people who qualify through disability, that is, a protected and often vulnerable population that is also the target of impersonation schemes; heightened-care practice is treated as an obligation of the work rather than as a courtesy
the agent's book spans a limited set of carriers and plans and nothing here assumes access to every plan in a service area; the limitation is disclosed to clients rather than hidden

renewal income is a lagging consequence of service quality and of decisions taken in prior plan years, so the book is treated as a maintained asset with a service obligation attached rather than as a set of closed sales

the beneficiary owns every coverage decision; everything in this knowledge base is procedural knowledge for the agent's own practice and never personalized medical, financial, tax, legal or insurance advice to a consumer
exclusions: obtaining and maintaining the license, the annual certification class and the carrier contracts and appointments, and the process of getting appointed or contracted (covered by the certifications, contracts and compliant marketing KB); this KB only monitors the status of that stack as a condition that keeps renewals payable and servicing permissible

the marketing and communication rule catalog itself, including permission-to-contact mechanics, scope-of-appointment mechanics, the prohibited-practice list, advertising and material review, third-party marketing relationships, events and lead generation to non-clients (covered by the certifications, contracts and compliant marketing KB); this KB carries only the per-client permission state and the trigger test that says when the marketing stack applies

the agency-wide documentation, audit, call-recording, retention-schedule and regulatory complaint-response program (covered by the certifications, contracts and compliant marketing KB); only the longitudinal per-client service record and the relationship-level service-recovery response live here

enrollment-period classification, eligibility determination, needs intake at the point of sale, coverage-route comparison mechanics, drug and network comparison modeling, the enrollment conversation itself and its per-enrollment case file (covered by the enrollment periods, plan comparison and needs fit KB); when a genuine election right appears this KB packages the documented need and hands it off

personalized medical, financial, tax or legal advice of any kind; therapeutic questions belong to the prescriber and pharmacist, benefit determinations belong to the plan, and assistance-program eligibility belongs to the administering agency
acting as a beneficiary's authorized representative in an appeal or grievance, arguing claim adjudication, or negotiating balance bills with providers

any specific commission amount, renewal rate or fraction, recoupment window length, payment date, premium, cost-sharing figure, persistency benchmark or book-valuation multiple stated as current fact; every one is treated as a mechanism whose current value must be read from the current-year regulated schedule, the carrier's own contract and official sources for the agent's own state

steering a client toward a change, a stay or a particular carrier because of what the agent is paid, refreshing clients into equivalent plans to restart a compensation cycle, and any retention practice that uses fear, manufactured urgency, obstruction or a family member as leverage
servicing or discussing any plan the agent is not currently licensed, certified and appointed for, and contacting any person outside their recorded permission state
valuing, brokering or drafting the sale of a book of business, which is a contract-dependent and negotiated matter requiring counsel

competency_questions.question: How does compensation on an already-enrolled member actually come to exist, what decides whether an enrollment pays at the initial-year or the renewal-year rate, and how do I verify this plan year's terms instead of carrying last year's forward?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPENSATION_MECHANISM_MAP describes payer, payment path, rate-year determination and accrual as mechanisms with a current-year source and verification date per entry, and states no rate as fact

competency_questions.question: What has to stay simultaneously true, year after year, for the renewals on my existing book to keep paying, and which of those conditions can fail silently?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RENEWAL_CONTINUATION_CONDITIONS lists the condition classes with an expiry calendar and lead times, and AGENT_OF_RECORD_AND_ORPHANS explains how member-level credit is held, lost and disputed

competency_questions.question: When can compensation already paid be taken back, how do I run the book so a normal recoupment cycle is survivable, and how do I tell whether the book is actually stable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHARGEBACK_EXPOSURE_MANAGEMENT names the recoupment classes, the avoidable/unavoidable split and the reserve rule as a mechanism, and PERSISTENCY_AND_BOOK_ECONOMICS supplies cohort persistency with cause-coded attrition

competency_questions.question: How do I confirm the carrier actually paid me for every member I serve, at the rate year the rules require, and what do I do about a difference in either direction?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STATEMENT_RECONCILIATION defines the member-level comparison, the difference classes and the dispute evidence, including the duty to report an overpayment rather than keep it

competency_questions.question: If I move my contracts to another upline, consolidate carriers, sell the book, retire, or become unable to work, what happens to the renewal stream and who services my clients?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_PORTABILITY_AND_CONTINUITY treats release, assignability and successor payment as contract terms to be located and dated per carrier, and requires a written service-continuity plan with an activation trigger

competency_questions.question: A client calls with a problem: how do I decide in the first minutes what kind of problem it is, how urgent it is, who actually owns it, and where my own lane ends?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_REQUEST_TRIAGE supplies the event-class taxonomy, urgency rule, ownership routing and escalation ladder; SERVICE_SCOPE_BOUNDARY states the outer edge of the agent's lane; LONGITUDINAL_CLIENT_RECORD says what the interaction must leave behind

competency_questions.question: A client's doctor or hospital is leaving the plan's network in the middle of the year: what do I verify, what may I say, and when does this stop being a service problem?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROVIDER_DISRUPTION_RESPONSE requires two-source verification before reassurance and explains in-plan mechanisms as classes to confirm; SERVICE_VS_ELECTION_TRIAGE supplies the gate that decides when the question is handed to the enrollment lane

competency_questions.question: A client's prescription was rejected at the pharmacy or their drug cost jumped: what is the response sequence, and where does my role stop and the prescriber's begin?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DRUG_COST_EVENT_RESPONSE gives the counter-level diagnosis, current-year formulary verification, the exception and transition mechanisms as classes, and routes every therapeutic question to the prescriber or pharmacist

competency_questions.question: A claim was denied or an unexpected bill arrived: what can I actually do, what must I hand off, and what would make me a representative I am not authorized to be?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DENIAL_AND_BILLING_ESCALATION distinguishes the document classes, confirms coverage status, explains the plan's grievance and appeal routes as classes with deadlines to confirm, and states the authorization line the agent does not cross

competency_questions.question: When a mid-year problem appears, how do I decide between fixing it inside the current plan and moving the client, and how do I prove that decision had nothing to do with what I am paid?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_VS_ELECTION_TRIAGE requires the in-plan route to be exhausted and evidenced first and produces a dated client-side reason, and COMPENSATION_NEUTRALITY_IN_RETENTION makes the no-steering rule provable from the file

competency_questions.question: The annual plan-change documents just published: how do I turn them into a prioritized outreach plan instead of touching the whole book the same way?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLAN_CHANGE_DOCUMENT_TRIAGE extracts per-plan material changes and intersects them with member records to rank by member-level impact, and BOOK_SEGMENTATION_AND_SERVICE_CADENCE supplies the tiers and the capacity the plan must fit

competency_questions.question: What exactly is an annual review, what makes it compliant, and at what moment does it turn into a sales appointment with its own prerequisites?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANNUAL_REVIEW_PRACTICE states the agenda, treats a no-change outcome as a first-class result, and names the trigger test and prerequisites that apply when the conversation turns to another plan; SERVICING_CONTACT_BOUNDARY supplies the permission state the outreach depends on

competency_questions.question: How do I keep clients without pressuring them, what do I do when a client decides to leave anyway, and how does good service turn into new business I am allowed to accept?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETENTION_THROUGH_SERVICE_QUALITY names the prohibited persuasion moves and the clean-exit practice, SERVICE_RECOVERY_PROTOCOL supplies the repair sequence and cause coding, and REFERRAL_GROWTH_COMPLIANT requires the referred person's own permission before outreach

competency_questions.question: A long-standing client is becoming confused on calls and an adult child has started answering the phone: how do I keep serving them safely and lawfully?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VULNERABLE_CLIENT_CARE_PROTOCOL supplies the pace, teach-back, capacity-doubt pause, verified-authorization rule and the exploitation-alerting route, and requires the authorization state to be dated in the client record

glossary.definition: The payment a carrier makes to the agent of record for a member who remains enrolled beyond the initial year, under a schedule that regulated maximums and the carrier's own contract together determine; it is a mechanism, not a fixed number, and its current-year terms must be read from the carrier's published schedule and the current official rules.

The rule that decides whether a given enrollment pays at the initial-year or the renewal-year rate; it follows the beneficiary's own enrollment history and the relationship between the plan types involved, not how new the client is to this agent, which is why an agent can write a brand-new client and be paid at a renewal rate.

The reversal of compensation already paid when a defined condition occurs, such as an enrollment that never effectuates, a disenrollment inside the early window the current-year rules define, a retroactive termination, or death; the classes and windows are contract- and plan-year-specific and must be verified rather than assumed.

The carrier's record of which agent is credited with a member, established by the writing identifiers carried on the accepted application and lost when a later enrollment carries different identifiers; renewal payment and much of the servicing relationship follow this record rather than the client's own sense of who their agent is.

An enrolled member whose original agent is gone and whom a carrier assigns to another agent for servicing; they arrive with a service obligation but no relationship, often no recorded permission to contact, and compensation treatment set by the carrier's own rules rather than by the receiving agent's assumption.

The share of a defined cohort of members still in force after a stated interval, measured on the agent's own book with attrition coded by cause; it is a diagnostic for where service is failing, never a target that is allowed to reach a client conversation.

The class of document a plan issues before each new plan year describing what is changing in cost sharing, formulary placement, network and supplemental benefits, alongside the fuller coverage document; the agent's work is not reading it but intersecting it with each member's own drugs, providers and usage.

The distinction between contacting an existing client about the coverage they already hold and contacting anyone about a different plan or product; the second engages the marketing rule classes and their prerequisites, and the trigger test for the switch is applied before the outreach, not during the call.

The carrier-specific permission required before an agent's contract can be moved to a different upline or marketing organization; its terms, waiting conditions and effect on the existing book's renewal stream are contract clauses that must be located and dated per carrier rather than taken from a recruiter's summary.

Any mechanism that resolves a member's problem without changing plans, such as a coverage exception or appeal route, a transition supply, a preferred-pharmacy switch, a continuity-of-care provision, or a corrected enrollment record; exhausting the in-plan remedy is the gate that stands in front of every service-driven plan change.

nodes.definition: Fix in writing, before the first service call of the year, exactly which post-enrollment problems the agent owns and which belong to the plan, the prescriber, the pharmacist, the provider's billing office, a state health-insurance counseling program, or a public agency. The agent's lane is education about how the coverage the client already holds is supposed to work, verification of plan-published facts against current-year documents, orderly escalation through carrier channels, and documentation. It is not medical judgment, not legal or tax advice, not benefit adjudication, and not representation in an appeal. Writing the lane down converts a thousand improvised judgment calls into one repeatable routing decision, which is what allows an agent to be fast and genuinely useful without drifting into advice they are not licensed, authorized or insured to give.

included: the agent's own service lane and its outer edge
a routing map from each recurring problem class to its true owner
the authorization line for appeals and representation
the verify-then-answer rule for any plan-published fact
excluded: the marketing and communication rule catalog itself
enrollment-period and plan-comparison work
medical, legal or tax advice in any form
acting as an authorized representative in an appeal or grievance

pros.claim: A written lane makes fast help safe, because the agent can answer instantly inside it and route instantly outside it
pros.example: a client asking whether to stop a cholesterol drug because of its cost gets the cost mechanism explained and the clinical question routed to the prescriber in the same call

pros.claim: It protects the client from confident answers given by someone who is not the right source
pros.example: a coverage question about medical necessity is sent to the plan rather than guessed at from an old benefit summary

cons.claim: A hard boundary can feel like abandonment to a client who trusts the agent more than the plan's phone system
cons.example: a recently widowed client who wants the agent to just call the doctor's office and fix a bill hears a referral instead of an action

failure_modes: drifting into clinical, legal or tax opinions because the client asked and the agent knew a little
hiding behind the boundary to avoid genuinely owned work such as verifying a plan-published fact
routing without a warm handoff, so the client lands in a phone tree and never reaches an outcome
acceptance_tests: the scope statement names, for each recurring problem class, the owner, the agent's own action, and the handoff
a spot check of recent service notes shows no clinical, legal or tax opinion offered by the agent
every handoff in the sampled notes has a named destination and a follow-up date
revisit_triggers: a new problem class starts recurring in the intake log
a carrier changes which channel handles a class of issue
a service note shows a client acting on something the agent said outside the lane

base.update_signal: a regulator, carrier or state counseling program publishes updated guidance on what a licensed agent may do after enrollment, or the intake log shows a recurring problem class the current routing map does not cover

nodes.definition: Run the entire servicing relationship on the assumption that a meaningful share of the book is, or will become, vulnerable: older adults, people qualifying through disability, people with cognitive change, hearing or vision loss, limited English proficiency, or a caregiver making decisions in the room. The protocol is concrete practice rather than sentiment: measured pace and plain language, one topic per contact, teach-back before any action is taken, no same-call pressure to decide anything, written confirmation of what was agreed, verified authorization on file before anything is discussed with a family member, a documented pause and escalation when capacity is in doubt, and a known route for reporting suspected financial exploitation or a scheme impersonating the program the agent works within. It is a first-class obligation because the same population is the target of nearly every impersonation scam in this market.

included: pace, plain-language and teach-back practice on every substantive contact
the capacity-doubt pause and its escalation
verified caregiver or representative authorization before any disclosure
the no-pressure rule applied to service interactions
a route for suspected exploitation or impersonation schemes
excluded: clinical assessment of capacity, which belongs to a clinician
legal determinations about guardianship or power-of-attorney validity, which belong to counsel
the marketing rule catalog itself
making decisions on a client's behalf

pros.claim: Confirming understanding prevents the most damaging outcome in this business, a client who loses access to a doctor or a drug because they agreed to something they did not understand
pros.example: a teach-back at the end of a network-change call reveals the client believed their specialist was still covered

pros.claim: A dated authorization record ends the recurring argument about who may be told what
pros.example: an adult son calling for the third time is handled the same way every time because the file says what he is authorized to hear

cons.claim: Heightened care costs real time per interaction and cannot be compressed in the busiest weeks of the year
cons.example: a review that would take one call needs three because a caregiver must be authorized before anything substantive is discussed

failure_modes: treating a talkative adult child as authorized simply because they placed the call
reading a capacity concern as stubbornness and pressing on to a decision
documenting nothing, so a later dispute about what was understood has no record at all
recognizing an exploitation pattern and having no route to report it
acceptance_tests: every active client file records who may be spoken to, on what authorization, with a date
service notes for high-touch clients show a teach-back or a written confirmation step
a written route exists for reporting suspected exploitation or an impersonation scheme, with the destination named
revisit_triggers: a client's capacity, caregiver or authorization status changes
a scam or impersonation pattern targeting beneficiaries appears in the service log
a state or carrier updates its vulnerable-consumer or authorization guidance

base.update_signal: state or federal guidance on serving vulnerable consumers changes, or a client incident shows the current pace, authorization or reporting practice failed to protect someone

nodes.definition: Hold the rule that nothing the agent is paid may influence what the agent recommends, whether the recommendation is to change plans, to stay, or to do nothing, and build the practice so that the neutrality is provable rather than merely asserted. Post-sale is where steering is most tempting and least visible: a switch can restart a compensation cycle, a stay can protect a renewal, and a recoupment can be dodged by talking a client out of a change they are entitled to make. Neutrality in practice means the client's verified needs drive the recommendation, the compensation consequence is never a stated or unstated reason, the limited set of carriers the agent represents is disclosed, and the file carries a client-side rationale written before any compensation consequence was even considered.

included: the no-steering rule applied to stay, switch and do-nothing decisions
disclosure of the limited carrier set the agent can offer
a need-first rationale recorded before other considerations
the churn prohibition against moving clients to restart a compensation cycle
the mirror prohibition against obstructing a legitimate change to protect a renewal or avoid a recoupment
excluded: the compensation mechanics themselves, which are mapped separately
the point-of-sale comparison method
any judgment about whether a given regulated schedule is fair
carrier bonus program design

pros.claim: A client-side rationale written into the file is the only durable defense when a season's pattern of switches is later reviewed
pros.example: a review of a season shows every change traced to a named formulary or network event rather than to a carrier mix

pros.claim: Neutrality removes the internal argument that slows down every borderline decision
pros.example: an agent facing a recoupment on a member who should move makes the call in minutes because the rule already decided it

cons.claim: Strict neutrality sometimes requires an action that costs the agent income now for a reputational benefit that arrives slowly
cons.example: telling a client to stay put through the annual window when a change would have generated new compensation

failure_modes: annual refreshes of clients into equivalent plans with no need-based reason
quietly discouraging a change that would trigger a recoupment
letting carrier bonus or incentive structures shape which plans get discussed at all
recording client wanted a change as the entire rationale
acceptance_tests: every stay-or-switch recommendation in the file names the client-side reason before any other consideration
the season's change pattern can be explained plan by plan without reference to compensation
the limited-carrier-set disclosure appears in the client record
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes incentive or bonus structures
the change pattern concentrates in one carrier without a need-based explanation
a compensation rule change alters the stay-versus-switch economics

base.update_signal: a compensation or incentive rule change alters the stay-versus-switch economics, or an internal audit of a season's changes finds switches without a documented client-side reason

nodes.definition: Maintain, per client, the live state of the agent's right to contact them, and know precisely where a servicing contact becomes a marketing contact carrying its own prerequisites. An existing servicing relationship supports contact about the coverage the client already holds; it does not by itself authorize solicitation of a different product, and permissions narrow, expire or are revoked. The unit of work is a permission register that records how permission arose, what it covers, what channel it allows, what the client has opted out of, and when it lapses under current-year rules, plus the trigger test the agent applies before every outreach: if the purpose is to introduce a different plan or product, the marketing stack applies and its required artifacts must exist before that conversation starts, not after it has drifted there.

included: per-client permission state with its provenance and date
opt-outs and channel restrictions honored across the whole book
the servicing-versus-marketing trigger test applied before outreach
the rule that any outreach list is built from the register rather than from memory
excluded: the permission and appointment-scope rule catalog and its documentation mechanics
prospecting and lead generation to non-clients
event and advertising compliance
deciding what a plan may say in its own materials

pros.claim: A permission register makes an outreach list buildable in minutes and defensible afterwards
pros.example: an annual outreach list automatically excludes the clients who opted out of calls and routes them to their chosen channel instead

pros.claim: Applying the trigger test before the call prevents the most common drift in this business
pros.example: a service call about a premium question that would have wandered into a different plan is split into two properly prepared contacts

cons.claim: Conservative permission handling suppresses outreach to clients who would have welcomed it
cons.example: a client hit hard by a formulary change is reached late because their permission state was stale and had to be re-established

failure_modes: treating a years-old permission as permanently valid
letting a service call slide into introducing a different product without the required prerequisites
keeping opt-outs in someone's memory rather than in the register
building a campaign list from a spreadsheet export that ignores channel restrictions
acceptance_tests: every client record carries a dated permission state, its source, and any channel or topic restriction
a sampled outreach list reproduces from the register with no opted-out client on it
any campaign that mixes servicing and product-introduction purposes is split before it is sent
revisit_triggers: the marketing or contact rule class changes for a plan year
a client opts out or changes preferred channel
a planned campaign mixes servicing and product-introduction purposes

base.update_signal: the contact-permission rule class changes for the plan year, or an outreach is found to have reached a client outside their recorded permission state

nodes.definition: Build and keep current a map of how the agent is actually paid on each contracted plan class, expressed as mechanism rather than as remembered numbers: who pays and through what hierarchy, what determines whether a given enrollment pays at the initial-year or the renewal-year rate (a property of the beneficiary's own enrollment history and the relationship between the plan types involved, not of how new the client is to this agent), how payment accrues and is released including any effectuation requirement and cycle timing, which plan classes sit outside the regulated maximums and follow carrier-set or state-filed arrangements instead, and what documentation proves which rate was applied. Every entry carries the current plan-year source it came from and the date it was read, because last year's schedule is not evidence about this year's.

included: payer, hierarchy and payment path per contracted plan class
rate-year determination stated as a rule rather than a number
accrual, effectuation and release mechanics with cycle timing
which classes follow regulated maximums versus carrier or state-filed arrangements
a source reference and retrieval date on every entry
excluded: stating any current rate, maximum, fraction or amount as fact
carrier contracting and appointment paperwork
tax treatment of the income, which belongs to a tax professional
quoting compensation to a recruit or a client from memory

pros.claim: Knowing that rate year follows the beneficiary's history rather than the agent's relationship prevents both revenue surprises and false statements to clients
pros.example: an agent expecting an initial-year payment on a long-enrolled member who moved plans finds the renewal-rate rule already written on the map

pros.claim: A sourced map makes every downstream income model auditable instead of anecdotal
pros.example: a book projection that cites the schedule entry and the date it was verified rather than a number someone repeated at a meeting

cons.claim: The map goes stale every plan year and rebuilding it is unglamorous work that competes directly with selling season
cons.example: a schedule updated after the map was built leaves an entire plan class modeled on superseded mechanics

failure_modes: carrying last year's figures forward as if they were current fact
assuming every plan class in the book follows the same schedule
quoting compensation to a client or a recruit from memory
recording a number without recording where it came from
acceptance_tests: each contracted plan class has a mechanism entry naming its published source and the date it was verified
no entry states a rate, maximum or fraction as fact without a current-year source reference
the rate-year determination rule is written as a rule that can be applied to a new case
revisit_triggers: a carrier or regulator publishes next plan-year compensation terms
a new plan class or carrier is added to the book
a statement shows a rate the map does not explain

base.update_signal: a carrier or regulator publishes plan-year compensation terms, or a reconciliation finds a paid rate the map cannot explain

nodes.definition: Maintain the standing checklist of everything that must remain simultaneously true for the renewal stream on an existing book to keep paying, and put each item's expiry on a calendar with a lead time long enough to act. The classes are an active resident or non-resident license covering every state where members actually live, the current plan-year certification class completed for each carrier and product, an active and unsuspended appointment with each carrier, the member still enrolled and effectuated in a plan the agent is credited on, the agent-of-record credit intact, and the hierarchy through which payment flows unchanged or properly released. The reason this checklist exists is that its failures are silent: nothing announces that renewals stopped except a smaller statement several cycles later.

included: the continuation condition classes and their interaction
an expiry calendar with lead times per condition
the mapping from each condition to the members it would affect
a periodic confirmation that each condition still holds, with dates
excluded: how to obtain a license, complete a certification or get appointed
the compensation amounts themselves
member-level credit disputes, which belong to reconciliation
carrier internal payment processing

pros.claim: A calendar with lead time converts an invisible cliff into a routine task
pros.example: a non-resident license covering the one state where a handful of members moved is renewed before the deadline rather than discovered after a payment gap

pros.claim: Mapping conditions to affected members shows the size of each exposure before it materializes
pros.example: seeing that a single carrier appointment carries a large share of the book's renewal stream

cons.claim: The checklist is only as reliable as the member roster behind it, and rosters drift as people move and change plans
cons.example: a member who relocated to a state the agent is not licensed in sits unnoticed on the roster for a full plan year

failure_modes: assuming a certification completed for one carrier satisfies another
letting an appointment lapse in a state with few members and losing that state's renewals entirely
discovering a hierarchy change only from an unexplained payment gap
tracking expiries in memory rather than on a calendar with lead time
acceptance_tests: every condition class has a named owner, an expiry date and a lead-time reminder
a periodic check confirms each condition and records the date it was confirmed
each condition is mapped to the members whose renewals it controls
revisit_triggers: a member moves to another state
a carrier changes certification or appointment requirements
a payment gap appears without an obvious member-side cause

base.update_signal: a carrier or state changes licensing, certification or appointment requirements, or a renewal payment stops without a member-side explanation

nodes.definition: Manage the credit link between the agent and each member: established when the accepted application carries the agent's writing identifiers correctly, lost when a later enrollment carries different identifiers or when a member is re-enrolled through a channel that does not preserve them, and contested through a carrier process that accepts specific evidence and ignores everything else. The same node carries the mirror case, orphan members a carrier assigns after their original agent leaves, who arrive with a servicing obligation, no relationship, frequently no recorded permission to contact, and compensation treatment set by the carrier's own rules rather than by the receiving agent's assumption. The work product is a reconciled roster: who the carrier believes is credited, who the agent believes is credited, and a worked case for every difference.

included: writing-identifier accuracy at submission and at any re-enrollment
the credit-loss classes and how each becomes visible
the carrier dispute path and the evidence it actually accepts
orphan assignment, its servicing duty and its contact-permission gap
roster reconciliation against each carrier's portal
excluded: enticing another agent's client to move in order to capture credit
the enrollment submission mechanics themselves
litigation over commissions, which belongs to counsel
treating an orphan list as a prospecting list

pros.claim: A reconciled roster surfaces credit losses in the cycle they happen instead of at the end of a plan year
pros.example: a member re-enrolled through a call center shows up as a roster difference before the next renewal cycle closes

pros.claim: Knowing what evidence a carrier's dispute process accepts turns a complaint into a case that can actually be decided
pros.example: submitting the dated application record the process asks for rather than a narrative about the relationship

cons.claim: Chasing credit disputes consumes hours with uncertain outcomes and can strain a carrier relationship
cons.example: a well-documented dispute that still resolves against the agent because the member signed a later application

failure_modes: treating an assigned orphan block as a lead list rather than a servicing obligation with a permission gap
letting writing identifiers be entered from memory during the busiest weeks
assuming a member who still calls the agent is still credited to the agent
opening disputes without the evidence the carrier's process requires
acceptance_tests: the agent's roster reconciles to each carrier's credited roster with every difference carrying a status
orphan members are recorded with their assignment date, servicing status and contact-permission state
each open dispute names the evidence submitted and the date it was submitted
revisit_triggers: a roster difference appears in a reconciliation cycle
a carrier changes its orphan-assignment or dispute process
a member reports contact from another agent

base.update_signal: a carrier changes how credit is assigned, disputed or reported, or a reconciliation cycle shows a pattern of credit losses concentrated in one channel

nodes.definition: Treat recoupment as a normal, modelable feature of the business rather than an accident. Compensation already paid can be reversed under defined classes: an enrollment that never effectuates, a disenrollment inside the early window the current-year rules define, a retroactive termination for non-payment or loss of eligibility, a change made through another agent, and death. The work is threefold. Know which classes apply to each contracted plan class and where their current-year terms are published. Reduce avoidable exposure at the source by enrolling only on verified fit, confirming effectuation, and setting accurate expectations at the point of sale. Hold a reserve so that a normal recoupment cycle is a planned line item rather than a cash crisis, where the reserve is a policy mechanism, a defined portion of new-enrollment compensation held until the exposure window closes, and never a promised figure.

included: recoupment classes per contracted plan class and where their current-year terms live
the avoidable versus unavoidable exposure split
effectuation confirmation as a routine step
the reserve rule expressed as a mechanism
the servicing duty that survives a recoupment
excluded: stating any window length, percentage or amount as fact
discouraging a client from a legitimate change in order to avoid a recoupment
carrier accounting practice
disputing every recoupment as if it were an error

pros.claim: A reserve policy turns the most predictable cash shock in this business into a planned line
pros.example: a season with several early disenrollments after one plan narrowed its network is absorbed without borrowing

pros.claim: Coding recoupments by cause separates the avoidable ones from the structural ones
pros.example: seeing that most reversals came from enrollments that never effectuated rather than from client dissatisfaction

cons.claim: Reserving withholds usable cash from an agent whose income is already concentrated in a short season
cons.example: holding back part of a strong season's compensation during the quietest months of the year

failure_modes: spending new-enrollment compensation as though it were final
treating every recoupment as an error to dispute rather than a modeled outcome
letting fear of a recoupment leak into what a client is told
assuming one carrier's window applies to another carrier's plans
acceptance_tests: each contracted plan class has its recoupment classes recorded with a current-year source and a verification date
a written reserve rule exists and the held balance is reconciled each cycle
recoupments are coded by cause so that avoidable ones are visible as a group
revisit_triggers: a carrier publishes changed recoupment terms
recoupments cluster in one plan or one enrollment channel
a season's recoupment experience departs from the modeled band

base.update_signal: a carrier revises its recoupment conditions or windows, or a season's recoupment experience falls outside the band the reserve rule assumed

nodes.definition: Reconcile each carrier's compensation statement against the agent's own roster every cycle, because the statement is the only place where credit loss, a wrongly applied rate year, a missed renewal, a duplicated or misapplied recoupment, and a plan-type reclassification become visible, and every one of them quietly reduces income until somebody looks. The work is a repeatable member-level comparison: members expected against members paid, rate year expected under the mapped rule against rate year applied, each recoupment matched to a named cause and window, and a case opened for every unexplained difference carrying exactly the evidence the carrier's process accepts. Differences run in both directions, and an overpayment that is discovered has to be reported rather than quietly kept.

included: cycle-by-cycle member-level statement-to-roster comparison
the difference classes and the evidence each requires
the dispute case file and its follow-up
self-reporting of overpayments
feeding confirmed differences back into the compensation map
excluded: computing what a rate should be from memory instead of from the mapped source
tax and accounting treatment of the income
carrier internal accounting
disputing a difference before its cause has been identified

pros.claim: Systematic reconciliation recovers income that nobody else in the chain has an incentive to find
pros.example: an entire plan's members paid at the wrong rate year for two cycles, caught only because the map said which rule applied

pros.claim: Member-level differences point straight at their cause instead of leaving a total to argue about
pros.example: a shortfall that resolves into three specific members whose credit moved rather than a vague missing amount

cons.claim: Reconciliation is monotonous cycle after cycle and mostly finds nothing, which is exactly when it stops being done
cons.example: three quiet cycles leading to a skipped check in the cycle that contained the error

failure_modes: reconciling totals rather than member-level detail
keeping an overpayment because the carrier has not noticed it
opening disputes without the evidence the carrier's process requires
letting a known difference age past the carrier's dispute window
acceptance_tests: every cycle has a reconciliation record listing member-level differences and their status
each difference is coded to a class and either resolved or escalated with dated evidence
any overpayment found is reported with a dated record of the report
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes statement format or payment cadence
differences cluster in one plan class or one carrier
a rate-year rule on the compensation map changes

base.update_signal: a carrier changes its statement format, payment cadence or dispute window, or a reconciliation cycle uncovers a difference class the current comparison does not detect

nodes.definition: Understand, before it matters, what happens to renewals and to clients when the agent's contractual position changes: moving to a different upline or marketing organization, which generally requires a release under the carrier's own rules and can suspend or redirect payment on the existing book; consolidating or terminating a carrier contract; selling or transferring a book, where assignability is a contract term and not a right; and incapacity or death, where whether renewals continue to an estate or a successor is likewise a contract term to be read rather than assumed. Running alongside the money question is a service obligation that does not pause: members are entitled to a serviced plan regardless of the agent's business changes, so a written continuity plan names who answers the phone and what activates them.

included: release mechanics as a contract class and their effect on the existing renewal stream
assignability and successor treatment as contract terms to locate and date
a pre-move checklist covering every carrier in the book
the service-continuity plan and the trigger that activates it
excluded: stating waiting periods, release terms or successor payment as universal fact
the contracting and appointment process itself
legal drafting or valuation of a sale or succession agreement
promising clients an outcome that depends on a carrier's discretion

pros.claim: Reading the release and assignment terms before a move prevents a decision that quietly cancels years of renewal income
pros.example: an agent considering an upline change discovers the release condition that would strand the existing book's renewals

pros.claim: A continuity plan protects clients from the one risk they never think about, which is the agent's own unavailability
pros.example: a covering agent named in advance who can answer a member's pharmacy emergency during a hospitalization

cons.claim: The terms are carrier-specific and change, so the analysis must be redone per carrier and cannot be generalized
cons.example: two carriers in the same book treating an identical hierarchy move in opposite ways

failure_modes: moving hierarchy on a recruiter's verbal assurance rather than on the written term
assuming a book is saleable because someone offered to buy it
leaving clients with no serviced contact after a business change
discovering a successor clause only when it is too late to act on it
acceptance_tests: for each carrier, the release, assignment and successor terms are located, quoted by reference and dated in the file
a written continuity plan names the covering agent, the trigger and the client notification method
revisit_triggers: an upline or marketing organization change is being considered
a carrier revises its contract, release or assignment terms
the agent's health, retirement plan or business structure changes

base.update_signal: a carrier revises its release, assignment or successor terms, or the agent begins contemplating a hierarchy move, a sale or a retirement date

nodes.definition: Keep one continuing record per client that outlives plan years and staffing changes: who may be contacted and under what authorization, the permission state and where it came from, the current plan and effective date, the verified provider and medication picture with the date each item was verified, every service contact with what was asked and what was done, every stay-or-switch recommendation with the client-side reason recorded before anything else, and the artifacts that show what was disclosed. This is the ongoing service file and it is deliberately distinct from the point-of-sale case file for a single enrollment. Its job is to make a multi-year relationship reconstructable when a client, a family member, a carrier or a reviewer asks what happened and why, at a moment when memory is worthless.

included: authorization and permission state with dates
plan history and effective dates
dated verification of providers, pharmacies and medications
a contact log with actions, owners and outcomes
the rationale trail behind every recommendation
excluded: the agency-wide records program, retention schedules, call-recording and audit-response design
the per-enrollment point-of-sale case file
storing clinical detail beyond what servicing actually requires
keeping data whose only purpose is marketing

pros.claim: A dated verification trail is the difference between we checked and an answer that holds up years later
pros.example: a client's belief that they were never told about a network change is answered with the dated note and the written confirmation that was sent

pros.claim: One continuing file makes any competent colleague able to serve the client during an absence
pros.example: a covering agent handling a drug rejection without re-interviewing a frightened member

cons.claim: The record only pays off later, so it is the first discipline abandoned under seasonal pressure
cons.example: a week of calls logged as one-line notes that explain nothing six months on

failure_modes: notes that record activity but never the reason for a recommendation
medication and provider data captured once and never re-dated
sensitive detail stored well beyond what servicing needs
parallel records in a notebook, a phone and a system that disagree
acceptance_tests: a sampled client file reconstructs the last plan year: contacts, verifications with dates, recommendations with their reasons
authorization and permission state are present and dated on every active file
no sampled file holds clinical or personal detail beyond what a servicing purpose explains
revisit_triggers: a client's authorization, plan, providers or medications change
a sampled file cannot answer why a past recommendation was made
a records, privacy or retention requirement changes

base.update_signal: a privacy, records or retention requirement changes, or a sampled file fails to reconstruct a plan year of contacts, verifications and reasons

nodes.definition: Put every inbound problem through one classification pass before doing anything else: what class of event is this (premium or billing, identification and plan access, pharmacy rejection or cost change, provider participation change, denial or unexpected bill, eligibility or assistance-status change, plan-year change notice, suspected scam or impersonation), how urgent is it in the client's own terms because out of medication today is not the same as a confusing letter, who genuinely owns it, what does the agent do right now, and what is the escalation path with a named channel, the evidence it requires and a promised follow-up date. Triage exists because the same call handled ad hoc takes several times as long, produces inconsistent answers across clients, and leaves nothing behind for the record.

included: the event-class taxonomy and how each class is recognized
an urgency rule keyed to client consequence rather than to caller volume
ownership routing to plan, prescriber, pharmacy, provider billing or public resource
the escalation ladder with channels and evidence
the follow-up commitment and the closure test
excluded: performing resolution steps that belong to the plan, prescriber or provider
anything outside the scope boundary
election-period analysis, which is handed to the enrollment lane when a real right exists
answering an unclassified problem because it seemed simple

pros.claim: Classification at the door lets access emergencies jump the queue while paperwork questions batch safely
pros.example: a pharmacy rejection with no pills left is worked the same hour while a benefit-letter question is scheduled for the next day

pros.claim: A promised follow-up date shifts the chasing burden from the client to the agent, which is where it belongs
pros.example: an elderly member who does not have to call three times to find out what happened

cons.claim: Any taxonomy invites forcing an unusual problem into the nearest available box
cons.example: a complaint about a marketing call from an unrelated caller logged as a billing issue and effectively lost

failure_modes: promising a resolution the agent does not control
recording no follow-up date, so the client has to chase the agent
closing a case at the handoff rather than at the client's outcome
letting the loudest caller set the queue instead of the urgency rule
acceptance_tests: each intake record carries an event class, an urgency level, an owner, a next action and a follow-up date
closure requires a confirmed client-side outcome rather than a completed handoff
the taxonomy has an other class that is reviewed rather than used as a dead end
revisit_triggers: a new event class appears repeatedly in the log
a carrier changes its escalation channel or evidence requirements
follow-up dates start being missed in a segment

base.update_signal: the intake log shows a recurring event class the taxonomy lacks, or a carrier changes the channel or evidence its escalation path requires

nodes.definition: Handle the most emotionally charged mid-year event with verification before reassurance. The sequence is fixed: confirm the change from the plan's current directory and from the provider's own office, because directories lag reality and office staff sometimes describe an unresolved contracting dispute as final; establish what the member actually needs, which is an active course of treatment, a scheduled procedure or a long relationship with a primary clinician rather than an abstract preference; explain the mechanisms that exist inside the current plan, such as continuity-of-care provisions where they apply, transition arrangements, out-of-network cost rules and prior-authorization implications, always as classes to be confirmed with the plan rather than as promises; document what was verified and when; and only then ask whether a genuine election right exists, which is a separate question that goes to the enrollment lane.

included: two-source verification of a participation change
a needs assessment focused on continuity of active care
in-plan mechanisms explained as classes to confirm with the plan
dated documentation of what was verified and said
the handoff test that opens the election question
excluded: negotiating with the provider or the plan on the member's behalf
guaranteeing that a continuity provision will be granted
election-period classification and plan comparison
clinical judgment about whether to change clinicians

pros.claim: Two-source verification prevents both false alarms and false comfort in the event clients panic about most
pros.example: a directory still listing a clinic whose own office confirms it stopped accepting the plan last month

pros.claim: Naming the in-plan mechanisms first keeps a frightening event from becoming an automatic plan change
pros.example: a member whose surgery proceeds under a continuity provision instead of a rushed switch mid-treatment

cons.claim: Verification takes days that a frightened client experiences as inaction
cons.example: a member with a scheduled procedure waiting while the plan and the provider's office give conflicting answers

failure_modes: repeating the plan's directory as fact
implying that a continuity provision applies before the plan has confirmed it
letting the disruption become an automatic reason to move the member
leaving no dated record of what the member was told during the panic
acceptance_tests: the file shows both verification sources with dates before any option was discussed
the member's continuity-of-care need is recorded before options are presented
any election question is handed off rather than answered inside the service call
revisit_triggers: a plan announces a network change affecting a whole segment
a provider group's contract status changes again
a continuity mechanism the file relied on is denied in practice

base.update_signal: a plan changes its network or continuity-of-care provisions for the plan year, or a case shows the two-source verification step producing a wrong answer

nodes.definition: Work the drug-cost event class with a fixed sequence that never crosses into clinical territory. Establish what actually happened at the counter, which is a rejection, a prior-authorization or step-therapy requirement, a quantity limit, a tier or formulary placement change, a pharmacy outside the plan's preferred arrangement, or a coverage-phase transition that changed the member's share. Verify the current-year formulary and pharmacy rules from the plan's own current documents rather than from last year's memory. Explain the mechanisms that exist, including the plan's coverage-determination and appeal routes, transition-supply rules for a member new to a plan or affected by a formulary change, preferred-pharmacy and mail-order differences, and assistance-program screening, always as classes the member or the prescriber can pursue. Route every therapeutic question, whether about alternatives, substitutions or stopping a drug, to the prescriber or pharmacist. Then document what was verified and what the member was told.

included: counter-level diagnosis of what the rejection or cost change actually was
current-year formulary and pharmacy verification from plan documents
coverage determination, appeal and transition-supply routes as classes
assistance-program screening and referral
prescriber and pharmacist routing for every clinical question
dated documentation
excluded: recommending, substituting or discouraging any medication
predicting the outcome of an exception request
determining assistance-program eligibility, which belongs to the administering agency
the enrollment-stage drug cost modeling used to compare plans

pros.claim: A fixed sequence turns a panicked pharmacy call into a same-day set of concrete next steps owned by the right party
pros.example: a rejection identified as a prior-authorization requirement, with the request routed to the prescriber's office that afternoon

pros.claim: Verifying the current-year formulary stops the agent from repeating a cost that no longer exists
pros.example: a tier that changed at the start of the plan year and explains the whole complaint

cons.claim: Nothing in the sequence guarantees the member gets the drug at the price they expected, and the agent absorbs that disappointment personally
cons.example: an exception request denied after the member was told only that the route existed

failure_modes: speculating about clinical alternatives in order to save the member money
quoting a cost or tier from a superseded formulary
treating a mid-year cost shock as an automatic reason to change plans
leaving the member to chase the prescriber's office alone with no follow-up date
acceptance_tests: the file records the counter-level cause, the current-year source verified with its date, and the routed owner of each next step
no service note contains a therapeutic recommendation made by the agent
each routed step carries a follow-up date and a recorded outcome
revisit_triggers: a plan issues a mid-year formulary change
the same drug event class recurs across several members
transition-supply or coverage-determination rules change for the plan year

base.update_signal: a plan changes formulary, transition-supply or coverage-determination rules, or a case shows the agent's explanation of a route did not match how the plan actually handled it

nodes.definition: Meet the denial-or-bill event with orientation rather than representation. The agent's work is to read the document with the member and identify what it actually is, because a plan denial, a statement of benefits that is not a bill, a provider balance bill, a coordination-of-benefits problem and a retroactive eligibility issue look alike to a frightened person and have entirely different owners; to confirm coverage status and effective dates from the plan's own record; to explain the plan's published grievance and appeal routes and their deadline classes as things the member must confirm with the plan; to point toward the free counseling and advocacy resources that exist for beneficiaries; and to document all of it. Acting as the member's representative in an appeal requires a formal authorization the agent generally does not hold and must not assume; getting the member to the right channel quickly is simultaneously the limit of the role and most of its value.

included: identification of the document class
confirmation of coverage status and effective dates from the plan record
grievance and appeal routes and deadline classes explained as things to confirm
referral to free counseling and advocacy resources
escalation through a carrier's agent-support channel where one exists
documentation and outcome follow-up
excluded: filing or arguing an appeal as the member's representative without a documented authorization
interpreting medical necessity
negotiating with providers or collectors
legal advice about a balance bill or a collections notice

pros.claim: Correctly identifying that a document is not a bill resolves a large share of these events in a single call
pros.example: a statement of benefits mistaken for an invoice, defused before the member pays it

pros.claim: Naming the deadline class early keeps a member from losing a route by waiting
pros.example: a member told at first contact to confirm the appeal window with the plan rather than after a month of provider calls

cons.claim: The agent is visible and the plan is not, so frustration lands on the agent while the remedy sits elsewhere
cons.example: a member who blames the agent for a provider's balance bill the plan never controlled

failure_modes: drafting appeal arguments the agent is not authorized to make
stating a deadline from memory instead of pointing to the plan's own statement of it
closing the case at the referral without checking whether the member reached an outcome
treating a denial as evidence that the plan was the wrong choice
acceptance_tests: the record shows the document class, the coverage status confirmed, the route explained and the follow-up outcome
no file shows the agent acting as a representative without a documented authorization
every referral to an external resource names the resource and the date it was given
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its grievance or appeal channel
denial events cluster in one plan or one provider group
an authorization to represent a member is offered and must be assessed

base.update_signal: a carrier or regulator changes the grievance, appeal or representation rules, or a case shows a member lost a route because of how the agent explained it

nodes.definition: Treat a dissatisfied client as two events at once: an individual repair and a signal about the practice. The repair is procedural rather than emotional improvisation: acknowledge without defensiveness, restate the client's account back to them until they agree it is right, separate what the agent controlled from what the plan or provider controlled without using that separation as an excuse, fix what is fixable, say plainly what is not, and confirm in writing what will happen next and by when. The signal is analytic: code the dissatisfaction by cause, distinguishing a verification the agent skipped, an expectation set too high at enrollment, a carrier process failure and a plan design the client never understood, then let clusters change the practice. Formal complaint handling that reaches a carrier's complaint process or a regulator carries its own required procedure and belongs to the compliance program; what lives here is the relationship and the pattern.

included: the repair sequence and its written next-step confirmation
cause coding of every dissatisfaction event
cluster analysis that feeds a practice change or an explicit decision not to change
the escalation decision that hands an event to the compliance program
excluded: the regulatory complaint-response procedure, its filings, deadlines and audit documentation
paying or inducing a client to withdraw a complaint
withdrawing service from a client who complained
arguing the client out of their account of what happened

pros.claim: A clean repair often produces a more loyal client than one who never had a problem, and always produces a better record
pros.example: a missed callback during the annual season repaired with a written recap and a standing check-in the client actually wanted

pros.claim: Cause coding turns individual complaints into the only reliable map of where the practice leaks
pros.example: three unrelated complaints that all trace back to reviews run without re-verifying medications

cons.claim: Cause coding surfaces uncomfortable findings about the agent's own process and is easy to quietly soften
cons.example: a cluster caused by rushed reviews recorded instead as isolated client misunderstandings

failure_modes: explaining the carrier's process instead of acknowledging the client's experience
one-off apologies with no cause code, so the same failure repeats next season
escalating to the compliance program too late to meet a required deadline
treating a vulnerable client's confusion as the cause rather than the effect
acceptance_tests: each dissatisfaction event carries a cause code, a written next-step confirmation and a closure note
cluster review happens on a stated cadence and names at least one practice change or an explicit no-change decision
events that meet the compliance program's criteria are escalated with a dated handoff
revisit_triggers: a cause-code cluster crosses the stated threshold
a complaint reaches a carrier or regulator channel
the same client raises a second issue within a short period

base.update_signal: a cause-code cluster appears that the current repair sequence does not address, or a complaint reaches a carrier or regulator channel and reveals a gap in the escalation criteria

nodes.definition: Apply an explicit gate to every mid-year problem and every review finding: can this be resolved inside the plan the client already holds, and has that route actually been exhausted rather than merely considered? Most drug-cost shocks, network surprises, billing confusions and access frictions have an in-plan remedy, and the plan change that looks like a clean fix frequently imports a new set of problems while restarting a compensation cycle, which is precisely the appearance the practice must avoid. Only when the in-plan route is exhausted or genuinely unavailable, and the client's own verified needs point elsewhere, does the question become an election question, at which point it is handed to the enrollment lane with the documented need attached. The gate's output is a dated, client-side written reason that survives review by someone who was not there.

included: the exhaust-the-in-plan-remedy-first rule
evidence that the in-plan route was actually attempted and what it returned
the handoff package delivered to the enrollment lane
the dated client-side written reason
a periodic anti-churn check across the whole book
excluded: enrollment-period classification, eligibility determination and plan comparison mechanics
discouraging a client who has made an informed decision to change
weighing any compensation consequence inside the gate
using the gate to delay a client past a closing window

pros.claim: Exhausting the in-plan route first solves most problems faster than any plan change could and leaves the rest of the client's coverage undisturbed
pros.example: a tier increase resolved by a coverage determination rather than by a move that would also have changed the client's specialist network

pros.claim: A dated client-side reason makes the whole season's change pattern explainable to a reviewer
pros.example: every switch in a season traced to a named event in the client's own record

cons.claim: The rule can slow a client who genuinely needs to move and is already inside a narrow window
cons.example: a coverage determination pursued for weeks while an election opportunity quietly closes

failure_modes: treating the annual window as an occasion to move clients rather than to review them
recording client wanted a change as the entire reason
using the gate to block a change the client has already decided on
skipping the gate when the in-plan remedy looks tedious
acceptance_tests: every plan change originating from a service event carries a record of the in-plan route attempted and what it returned
the written reason is client-side and dated before the change is executed
a periodic review of the book's changes finds no cluster without matching client-side events
revisit_triggers: a season's change volume rises without a matching pattern of client-side events
an in-plan remedy class stops working across a carrier
a plan or carrier exits a service area, which changes the gate's default answer

base.update_signal: an in-plan remedy class stops working across a carrier, or an audit of the season's changes finds moves whose in-plan route was never attempted

nodes.definition: When plan-year change documents publish, convert them into an impact map before a single review is scheduled. For each plan in the book, extract what materially changed in cost-sharing structure, formulary placement of commonly used drugs, network composition, supplemental benefits, service-area boundaries, and whether the plan is being discontinued or consolidated. Then intersect those changes with what the client records actually say about each member's providers, medications and usage. The output is a ranked outreach list: members whose specific circumstances are hit hardest first, members facing a plan termination or service-area exit next, and the untouched majority into a lighter touch. Reading the documents is bulk work that anyone can do; the entire value sits in the intersection with the record, which is why record quality decides the quality of the ranking.

included: per-plan extraction of material changes
intersection of changes with member-level records
ranking by member-specific impact
identification of terminating, consolidating or exiting plans
the outreach list handed to the review process
excluded: next-year plan comparison and recommendation, which belongs to the enrollment lane
marketing use of the change data
contacting any member outside their recorded permission state
assuming an unchanged plan needs no contact at all

pros.claim: Impact ranking puts the harmed clients first instead of processing the book in whatever order it was stored
pros.example: members whose maintenance drug moved tiers are reached before members with no material change at all

pros.claim: The map turns a mountain of documents into a finite, assignable work list
pros.example: a book across several plans reduced to a ranked list a single agent can actually work through

cons.claim: The intersection is only as good as the record, so stale medication and provider data produce a confident but wrong ranking
cons.example: a member ranked low because their record still lists drugs they stopped taking two years ago

failure_modes: reading only the summary page and missing a network or service-area change
ranking by the value of the member rather than by the impact on the member
starting outreach before the permission state has been checked
treating a plan with no changes as a segment that needs no contact
acceptance_tests: each plan in the book has a dated change digest naming its material changes and their source document
the outreach list is ranked by member-level impact and reconciled against the permission register
members in a terminating or exiting plan appear at the top of the list regardless of other factors
revisit_triggers: a plan issues a correction to its change documents
a plan termination or service-area change is announced
record staleness is discovered while working the list

base.update_signal: a plan corrects or reissues its change documents, or working the list reveals that the record fields the intersection depends on are systematically stale

nodes.definition: Run the annual review as a structured service conversation with a fixed agenda: confirm who is on the call and what authorization applies, re-verify the medication list, the treating providers and the pharmacy, walk the client through what their own plan is changing for the coming year in terms that mean something to them, ask what has changed in their life and health, answer their questions, and record the outcome, including the frequent and entirely correct outcome that nothing should change. The review is simultaneously a compliance decision point: the moment the conversation turns toward a different plan or a new product it becomes a sales appointment governed by the marketing rule classes, with prerequisites and artifacts that must exist before that part of the conversation continues. Knowing exactly where that line falls, and stopping to satisfy it rather than drifting across it, is the skill the whole season depends on.

included: the review agenda and its re-verification steps
the no-change outcome treated as a first-class result
the trigger test that converts a review into a sales appointment
the prerequisites obtained before crossing that line
the dated review record
excluded: the marketing rule catalog and appointment-scope mechanics themselves
plan comparison and enrollment execution
reviewing a plan the agent is not certified and appointed to discuss
using the review as a scheduled occasion to move clients

pros.claim: A fixed agenda makes reviews reproducible under seasonal load and produces the record that proves the review happened at all
pros.example: a review in the busiest week that still captures re-verified drugs, providers and a dated no-change decision

pros.claim: Re-verification at review time is what keeps every downstream impact map and recommendation honest
pros.example: a medication list corrected in the review that changes how the next plan-year impact ranking treats the member

cons.claim: The review can degenerate into a compliance ritual that the client experiences as form-filling
cons.example: a client interrupted for authorization steps before anyone has asked how they have been

failure_modes: sliding from review into introducing a different plan without satisfying the prerequisites first
treating a no-change outcome as a failed review
reviewing from memory rather than from the client record
compressing reviews so far that re-verification is skipped
acceptance_tests: every completed review has a dated record with re-verified drugs and providers, the changes discussed and the outcome
no review record shows a different plan discussed without the required prerequisites recorded first
no-change outcomes are recorded with their reason rather than left blank
revisit_triggers: the marketing or appointment-scope rule class changes for the plan year
a review record shows the sales-appointment line crossed without prerequisites
the agenda misses a change class the book actually experienced

base.update_signal: the marketing or appointment-scope rule class changes for the plan year, or a sampled review record shows the sales-appointment line crossed without its prerequisites

nodes.definition: Divide the book into service tiers on need-based signals rather than on what each member is worth to the agent, then assign each tier a contact cadence that the agent can actually sustain across a full year. Signals that raise a member's tier include a complex medication list, a plan with unstable network or formulary behavior, a recent care transition or hospitalization, an assistance-status change, cognitive or communication difficulty, absence of caregiver support, and a history of unresolved service events. Assigning a cadence is a capacity commitment rather than an aspiration: the total planned touches across all tiers must fit the hours that exist outside the annual season, or the plan is fiction that will collapse onto the loudest clients. Segmentation also sets the order in which members are contacted when a plan change or termination event hits the book.

included: need-based tiering signals and how each is detected
a contact cadence per tier
reconciliation of planned touches against available hours
the priority order used during plan-change and termination events
periodic re-tiering as members change
excluded: tiering by compensation value or book value
using a tier to withhold service a client has requested
marketing segmentation for prospecting
treating a tier as a permanent label

pros.claim: Need-based tiers put scarce hours where coverage failures actually happen
pros.example: members on many maintenance drugs get a mid-year check while a healthy member with stable coverage gets a lighter touch

pros.claim: Reconciling the cadence against real hours exposes an over-promised service model before clients discover it
pros.example: a planned quarterly touch for the whole book that turns out to require more hours than the year contains

cons.claim: Any tiering under-serves someone whose need is invisible in the data
cons.example: a quiet member whose cognitive decline surfaces only after a missed premium payment

failure_modes: planning a cadence that exceeds the hours that exist
tiering once and never re-tiering as members age and change
letting a tier become a ceiling on responsiveness to an inbound request
allowing compensation value to creep into the tiering signals
acceptance_tests: every active member carries a tier, the signal that set it and a date
planned touches per period reconcile to available capacity with the arithmetic shown
inbound requests are served on urgency regardless of tier
revisit_triggers: a member's health, plan or support situation changes
the agent's available capacity changes
an event class overwhelms the planned cadence

base.update_signal: capacity changes, or a period's actual touches diverge materially from the planned cadence for a whole tier

nodes.definition: Treat retention as an outcome produced upstream by accurate expectations set at enrollment, problems solved when they appear, and contact that arrives before the client has to chase it, never as a persuasion event staged when someone threatens to leave. The prohibited moves are named rather than left to judgment: manufactured urgency, fear framing about losing coverage, implying an official or governmental role, disparaging a competing plan instead of explaining mechanisms, obstructing or delaying a change the client has decided on, and using a family member as leverage. The matching positive practice is equally concrete: give a client the information they need to leave if leaving is right for them, make the exit clean, say the door stays open, and record it. A book that stays because leaving is hard is a liability waiting to become a complaint; a book that stays because leaving would be a loss is the asset this entire subdomain exists to build.

included: retention treated as an upstream service outcome
the named list of prohibited persuasion moves
the clean-exit practice and its record
a genuinely informational conversation when a client is considering leaving
the departure reason captured for learning
excluded: any pressure, urgency or fear tactic
inducements paid to clients for staying
obstructing or delaying an election the client has decided on
measuring retention, which is a separate unit of work

pros.claim: Clean exits generate referrals and returns in a way that pressured saves never do
pros.example: a client who moved out of the service area sending their neighbor because the handoff was handled gracefully

pros.claim: Naming the prohibited moves makes them checkable in a record instead of a matter of taste
pros.example: a sampled retention conversation reviewed against the list and found clean

cons.claim: Refusing pressure tactics means visibly losing clients that a more aggressive competitor would have kept
cons.example: a member moved by a call-center campaign the agent will not answer in kind

failure_modes: a save conversation that turns into an argument the client cannot win
framing a competing plan as dangerous rather than explaining its mechanisms
going silent after a client says they are leaving, which forfeits the relationship entirely
letting a family member be used to pressure the client into staying
acceptance_tests: sampled retention conversations contain no urgency framing, fear framing or competitor disparagement
every departure has a recorded reason and a clean handoff note
no record shows a change being delayed or obstructed after the client decided
revisit_triggers: departures cluster around one plan, one season or one service failure
